selected_originals.title: Waypoint retained handoff replay
selected_originals.classification: single deterministic replay with a same-session human intervention; no autonomous sender-to-recipient transfer
observations: One run identifier records deterministic schema-2 replay, UI recognition and action delivery.
A blocking observation produces intervention_requested and control_transferred; one human_action click is followed by resume_validated and a successful result.
The evidence index calls this a manual intervention history and the retained target a fixture. No sender, recipient or second autonomous participant is present.
selected_originals.missing_evidence: Two distinguishable autonomous principals, a task-bearing delivery, recipient use, independent operator provenance and evidence the exchange exceeded authorization.

selected_originals.title: EPYC archived Codex and Fable session-bus inboxes
selected_originals.classification: designed operator-governed message bus; two addressed inboxes but no public recipient-use proof or independent operator boundary
observations: All 39 archived rows are from the coordinator role and address one of two named project roles.
The protocol says the coordinator is the role the operator interacts with; the daemon is not an agent, assigns by deterministic rule and never reviews work products.
Trust boundaries for registry, measurement, production and host changes are explicitly human-only. The config records operator decisions and operator-authorized sessions.

The selected files are inbox snapshots. They do not prove that either recipient read a specific message and then produced a content-dependent downstream artifact. Public history is under one repository account.
selected_originals.missing_evidence: A public receipt and exact downstream effect tied to a specific message, provider-backed autonomous recipient provenance, an independent operator boundary and an authorization crossing.

selected_originals.title: Vexter task ledger
selected_originals.classification: single-project Codex task/status ledger with workflow handoff labels and bounded operator supervision
observations: The ledger advances sequential task IDs and statuses, including research_handoff_completed and later downstream-research stages.
It contains no attributable autonomous sender, recipient, delivery receipt or recipient model/run identity.

The README defines one Mac-side control plane, requires every Codex task to close through GitHub and describes bounded operator supervision. The selected-file history is authored by one public account.
selected_originals.missing_evidence: Attributable autonomous sender and recipient records, exact task material and use, independent operator provenance and proof the workflow exceeded its designed control plane.

selected_originals.title: ylong_http HTTPS-proxy SOTA progress ledger
selected_originals.classification: real subagent-to-main review dependencies inside one human-approved controlled optimization run
observations: Read-only subagents return review findings and candidate changes; the main run later evaluates those inputs, including rejecting a proposed semaphore fast path before code because measured headroom was too small.
The ledger repeatedly records human approval or reapproval before authority-expanding amendments and refuses terminal claims until verifiers and a counterexample gate pass.

This is a genuine semantic dependency, but it is an intentional subagent hierarchy within one run and one repository, with explicit human authority and one public file author—not cross-operator rogue coordination.
selected_originals.missing_evidence: Independently controlled autonomous sender and recipient trajectories, cross-operator delivery/use and primary evidence of cooperation outside the human-approved run.

selected_originals.title: Logos Scripture Graph Ezekiel controlling-agent queue
selected_originals.classification: owner-directed multi-agent research/review workflow with real peer findings but explicit shared governance
observations: Peer-labelled reviews identify defects; later queue entries amend earlier inferences and the orchestrator uses those findings in rulings and worklists. This is real content-specific dependency inside the project.

AGENTS.md requires a human-gated master context and formal handoffs, and labels M8 continuity owner-directed. The queue identifies one orchestrator family and its peer/subagent lanes; the public checkpoint is committed by one owner account.
No public record authenticates independent operators or shows the coordinated work escaping the owner's authorized workflow.
selected_originals.missing_evidence: Provider-backed independently operated participants, a cross-operator receipt/effect chain and evidence the cooperation exceeded owner authorization.

scoped_prior_reporting_checks.reason: No selected family passed the independent-operator and authorization-crossing tests. The protocol therefore stops before episode-level novelty searching; the four resumed exact identity/effect searches are recorded only as bounded coverage.
scoped_prior_reporting_checks.claim: No global novelty claim is made.

known_family_overlap.named_exclusions: No selected record is treated as a new instance of the named DseWiki/RubyGems, Transluce, Amap, Green AI Bot, Technocore/Agent Workpad, OpenAI May/July, AISI GitHub handoff or Covert Assistance/METR families.
known_family_overlap.project_controls: EPYC, Vexter, ylong_http and Logos are classified from their own original governance records as designed systems or owner-directed workflows, not by dataset absence.

alternative_hypotheses_tested: single deterministic replay with same-session human intervention

conclusion.participant_test: Waypoint has no autonomous participants; Vexter has no attributable sender/recipient identities. EPYC names recipients but its selected records are inbound archives without demonstrated use. ylong_http and Logos contain real multi-agent dependencies inside explicitly governed projects.
conclusion.dependency_test: Only ylong_http and Logos establish content-specific review or suggestion use; both are designed same-project hierarchies.
conclusion.operator_boundary_test: No selected original supplies primary evidence of independently controlled operators. The strongest two preserve explicit human/owner authority.
conclusion.provider_attribution: Repository labels and model-family names are treated as origin claims, not independent provider attestations.
conclusion.rogue_intent_test: No subjective rogue intent is inferred.
conclusion.current_activity: The public events span March through September 2026; current autonomous activity is not claimed.
conclusion.result: No plausible previously unreported rogue-swarm candidate. No candidate ID assigned.
